summary.text: A 61-year-old woman with CKD from IgA nephropathy (diagnosed 1997) was treated with peritoneal dialysis for 70 months and then hemodialysis from 2020. During dialysis she developed secondary hyperparathyroidism refractory to cinacalcet, calcitriol and paricalcitol (PTH up to 690 pg/mL, phosphate 7.7 mg/dL, calcium 10 mg/dL, enlarged parathyroid glands). Two months before transplantation a selective right inferior parathyroidectomy showed parathyroid adenoma.

In 2020 she received a related living-donor kidney transplant (compatible blood group, identical HLA panel) without basiliximab induction, on corticosteroids, tacrolimus (switched to cyclosporine after two months) and mycophenolic acid.

About four months after transplant she was referred to a bone and mineral clinic with widespread joint/bone pain without signs of inflammation and progressively worsening ambulation. Work-up showed recurrent hypercalcemic hyperparathyroidism (calcium 10.7 mg/dL and PTH 130 pg/mL cited, calcium 11.2 mg/dL on blood tests), severe vitamin D deficiency, hypophosphatemia, renal phosphate wasting (FePI 30.6%), creatinine 1.1 mg/dL with eGFR 54, and elevated bone turnover markers; several values conflict between text and Table 1.

Imaging showed vertebral fractures of D6 and D7, lumbar osteoporosis (T-score -3.7) and femoral osteoporosis (T-score -2.9), an enlarged hyperfunctioning parathyroid (11 x 3 mm), left knee marrow edema on MRI, and bone rarefaction compatible with Looser zones on hip X-ray; X-rays of shoulders and right knee were negative for fractures. Skeletal scintigraphy showed focal tracer uptake, with conflicting site descriptions in the text.

Osteomalacia secondary to severe vitamin D deficiency was suspected (bone biopsy not performed; differential diagnoses of arthropathy, infection, osteonecrosis and neoplasm excluded) and cholecalciferol 60,000 IU per day was started, then calcifediol 0.266 mg monthly was added at six months without antiresorptive therapy. Authors consider the picture a combination of osteomalacia and persistent hyperparathyroid bone disease.

At six months she attended in a wheelchair with partial pain relief and significant knee marrow edema on MRI; by nine months she walked independently with crutches with significant pain relief and reduced marrow edema, and at 26 months she was fully independent without assistive devices.

Oral bisphosphonates were recommended but not begun because of the need for dental implants; they were recommended again and the patient agreed to start. At Table-labelled Month 39 PTH, calcium, bone turnover markers and lumbar/hip BMD showed partial improvement with persistent lumbar osteoporosis and femoral osteopenia, and after one year of bisphosphonate therapy bone turnover markers remained mildly elevated, hypercalcemic hyperparathyroidism persisted, lumbar T-score was -2.6 and Looser-zone rarefaction regressed.
